sections.h2: What the recorder's office does in a sale
sections.html:
In West Chester, this office takes in the deed that passes a house to its new owner, gathers the realty transfer tax owed, and holds the lasting land record. A deed that hasn't been recorded leaves the old owner on the public record, and a buyer's lender or a later purchaser may balk at that.

The office is the custodian of all land records and transfer indexes, going back to 1688. It also records mortgages, satisfactions, powers of attorney, subdivision plans and notary commissions. Tax money it collects goes on to the Commonwealth, the county's 73 municipalities and its 14 school districts. Nobody at the counter will draft a deed, hunt for liens or advise you legally. A title company or attorney does that work.

The office is at 313 W. Market Street, Suite 3302, West Chester. Call 610-344-6330. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but recording documents must be handed in by 4 p.m.

  • Same-day recording runs 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Same-day recording of large exhibits such as maps and subdivision plans stops at 3:00 p.m.
  • The search library stays open until 4:15 p.m.
  • Fees are due at the moment of recording, and the office won't record an unofficial copy of a document already on record.

Any paper filing should carry a self-addressed stamped envelope. Leave it out and the county supplies postage and bills you $2.00.

A standard deed costs $94.75 to record under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. That base covers one UPI, up to four pages, one notation fee and four names. A mortgage and a deed of correction carry the same base.

Chester County recording fees, effective December 1, 2025
DocumentBase fee
Deed$94.75
Re-recorded deed or mortgage$96.75
Deed in blank or relocation deed$183.50
Satisfaction, assignment, release, easement$81.75
Power of attorney$20.50
Miscellaneous document$40.50

Extras stack on top. A UPI costs $20.00 per number, a document that misses the PRIA formatting standards carries a $25.00 non-compliance fee, and each exhibit adds $5.00. The base fee already contains a $41.25 judicial administration charge set by the Department of Revenue.

The rate is 1% of the consideration or computed value, whichever is higher, with higher rates in three places: Malvern and Tredyffrin at 1.5%, and Coatesville at 2.5%. Ask the recorder for the combined state and local figure that applies to your deed.

State law makes grantor and grantee jointly liable for the tax, and certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestacy are exempt. Who covers the bill in a sale is a matter for the sales agreement.

  • Pay transfer tax with separate checks, one for the municipality and one for the state, made out to the Chester County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Only business checks, cashier's checks and money orders are taken for tax. Cash and credit cards are refused for tax.
  • Recording fees go on a third check or other accepted payment.

Payment errors and gaps on page one cause most returns. The recorder takes cash in person for recording fees only, and personal, estate and trustee checks are always refused. Checks older than 180 days are returned, no more than ten documents may share one check, and a returned check triggers a $25 bank fee on top of the $10.00 rejection fee for returned documents.

  • Type a valid UPI on the first page. A computer-printed label on page one is acceptable.
  • Give the grantee's exact mailing address and certify it with a signature, as 16 P.S. Section 9781 requires.
  • Attach a Statement of Value when the deed doesn't show the full value, unless a family exemption applies. The Common Level Ratio factor, updated each July 1, belongs on that form.
  • For land in more than one municipality, show the local tax split in dollars on the deed.
  • Match every name across the caption, signature and notary acknowledgment, including Sr., Jr. and III.

sections.h2: Checks before the deed goes in
sections.html:
Begin with the chain of title. Any mortgage you paid off ought to have a recorded satisfaction, and filing a missing one costs the $81.75 base fee in that category. A house inherited through an estate leans harder on the Statement of Value and the family-transfer rules, so get your title company looking at those early.

Check the grantee's mailing address with the buyer too. Future tax bills follow the address on the deed, and the county asks that it be exact, current, legible and scannable. A deed sent in with a tax check from a personal or estate account will be turned away, so arrange transfer tax funds as a cashier's check or money order ahead of time.

  • If the seller's copy of the vesting deed is lost, order one from the recording office. Staff-made certified copies run $0.50 per page plus $5.00 for certification.
  • Ask the title company whether the property sits in Malvern, Tredyffrin or Coatesville, where higher tax rates apply.
  • Confirm the deed shows the correct UPI and not the tax parcel number, since the two are formatted differently.

Yes. Simplifile and CSC eRecording both carry electronic filings to the Chester County office, and most title companies send closing packages that way. For a deed that owes tax, the consideration and the state and municipal tax amounts must appear on the first page.

Each package is limited to ten documents, and one document can list no more than ten UPI numbers. Deeds of correction, re-recorded deeds and Statements of Value with exhibits attached can't be e-recorded and go in on paper. Resubmitting a document costs a $10 return fee each time, and a document recorded in error isn't refunded.

Chester County sits in the Philadelphia metropolitan area, with West Chester as the seat and Coatesville as its only city. About 557,116 residents live across roughly 751 square miles, with 217,440 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied home value is $485,600, median household income is $127,208 and median gross rent is $1,763. Owners occupy 75.1% of homes. Transfer tax can differ sharply from one township to the next.

faqs.q: How long does it take to record a deed in Chester County?
faqs.a: Same-day recording is offered until 4:00 p.m. on business days, and e-recorded packages through Simplifile or CSC are the usual route for closings. Large plans must arrive by 3:00 p.m. for same-day handling.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Chester County transfer tax by credit card?
faqs.a: No. Transfer tax must be paid by business check, cashier's check or money order made out to the Chester County Recorder of Deeds. Credit cards may be used only for recording fees and copy requests, with a 3.5% in-person fee.

faqs.q: Do I need a Statement of Value to record a deed in Chester County?
faqs.a: Yes, when the deed doesn't show the full and complete value of the property, unless a family exemption applies. It is a Department of Revenue form and is recorded with the deed, so its pages count toward the recording fee.

faqs.q: Can the Recorder of Deeds correct a mistake in a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Not by editing it. A deed of correction costs $94.75 and needs a written explanation on page one, the book and page of the deed being fixed, a new acknowledgment and a Statement of Value. Deeds of correction can't be e-recorded.

faqs.q: Is the transfer tax the same everywhere in Chester County?
faqs.a: No. The base rate is 1% of consideration or computed value, but Malvern and Tredyffrin charge 1.5% and Coatesville charges 2.5%. Check the municipality where the house sits before you price a sale.
